text.name: Passwords kept in memory
text.titlePass: Windows does not keep sign-in passwords in memory
text.titleFail: Windows keeps sign-in passwords readable in memory
text.why: With this old setting on, malware with administrator rights reads the password of everyone signed in, straight from memory.
fix: Tell IT: nothing on a current PC needs this setting.
It is the value UseLogonCredential of the WDigest key shown in the details; it must be 0 or absent.

text.name: LSA protection
text.titleFail: LSA protection is not switched on in the registry
text.why: LSA protection keeps other programs out of the process that holds sign-in secrets. Windows 11 may turn it on by itself without this setting.
fix: Open Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation details.
Turn on Local Security Authority protection and restart.
If the switch is missing, tell IT: it can be set by policy.

absent.found: Not configured (off on Windows 10; Windows 11 may still turn it on)

text.name: Old sign-in protocols
text.titlePass: Only NTLMv2 is used for network sign-in
text.titleFail: The weak LM or NTLM protocol is still used
text.why: LM and the first NTLM are decades old: a password sent with them over the network can be recovered within hours.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > Security Options > Network security: LAN Manager authentication level.
Choose "Send NTLMv2 response only" or one of the stricter choices below it.

labels.1: Sends LM and NTLM, NTLMv2 if negotiated
labels.5: Sends NTLMv2 only, refuses LM and NTLM

absent.found: Not configured (Windows default: sends NTLMv2 only)

text.name: LM password hashes
text.titlePass: Windows does not store the weak LM form of passwords
text.titleFail: Windows stores the weak LM form of passwords
text.why: The LM form of a password is cracked in minutes. Anyone who copies the account database then has the passwords.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > Security Options and enable the LAN Manager hash setting under Network security.
Change the passwords of the accounts on this PC afterwards: the old form stays until then.

text.name: Remote use of local administrators
text.titlePass: Local administrators are limited over the network
text.titleFail: Local administrators have full rights over the network
text.why: With this limit off, one stolen local administrator password opens every PC that shares it, without anyone at the keyboard.
fix: Tell IT: this is the value LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy shown in the details.
It must be 0 or absent unless a management tool truly needs it.

text.name: Sign-ins kept for offline use
text.titlePass: Windows keeps no more sign-ins for offline use than usual
text.titleFail: Windows keeps more sign-ins for offline use than usual
text.why: Windows keeps a check value of recent work-account passwords to sign in without the network. Whoever copies the disk can guess passwords against each one kept.
fix: Tell IT: this is the value CachedLogonsCount shown in the details.
It must be 10 (the Windows default) or less; the security option is named Number of previous logons to cache.

text.name: CredSSP fallback
text.titlePass: Remote sign-ins cannot fall back to the flawed CredSSP
text.titleFail: Remote sign-ins may fall back to the flawed CredSSP
text.why: CredSSP passes your sign-in to Remote Desktop and other remote tools. Its old version lets an attacker in the middle run commands on the far end.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc > Administrative Templates > System > Credentials Delegation.
Set "Encryption Oracle Remediation" to Enabled, with Force Updated Clients or Mitigated.

text.name: Add-ins to the sign-in process
text.titlePass: Other programs cannot load into the sign-in process
text.titleFail: Other programs may load into the sign-in process
text.why: Malware with administrator rights can add itself to the process that handles passwords and copy each one typed. Blocking add-ins closes that door.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
Check first that no smart-card or sign-in software in use needs an add-in.
On a single PC, open gpedit.msc > Administrative Templates > System > Local Security Authority.
Set "Allow Custom SSPs and APs to be loaded into LSASS" to Disabled.

text.name: NTLM session security (outgoing)
text.titlePass: Outgoing NTLM sessions require NTLMv2 and 128-bit encryption
text.titleFail: Outgoing NTLM sessions may use weaker protection
text.why: NTLM still signs in to some file shares and older services. Requiring its strongest session protection stops a downgrade to weaker keys.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > Security Options.
In "Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) clients", tick both boxes.

text.name: NTLM session security (incoming)
text.titlePass: Incoming NTLM sessions require NTLMv2 and 128-bit encryption
text.titleFail: Incoming NTLM sessions may use weaker protection
text.why: Programs that connect to this PC with NTLM can ask for weak session keys. Requiring the strongest protection refuses them.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > Security Options.
In "Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) servers", tick both boxes.

text.name: Anonymous fallback for system services
text.titlePass: System services never fall back to anonymous sessions
text.titleFail: System services may fall back to anonymous sessions
text.why: A service that falls back to an anonymous session sends its traffic without the protection a signed-in session gives.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > Security Options.
Disable "Network security: Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback".

text.name: Signing of directory traffic
text.titlePass: Directory (LDAP) traffic is signed when possible
text.why: Unsigned directory traffic can be changed in transit, so an attacker could alter what this PC is told about accounts and groups.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
On a single PC, open secpol.msc > Local Policies > Security Options.
Set "Network security: LDAP client signing requirements" to Negotiate signing or Require signing.
